interpretation.claim: the cross-modal linear bridge survives down to a 0.6B TEXT tower. i2t R@1 0.356 against 0.433 for the matched 27B text tower on identical images at identical training scale: 82% retention at 45x fewer text-tower parameters. Shuffled control 0.002, chance 0.0002.
interpretation.why_this_rung: the browser plan's standing blocker was that no sub-3B rung existed and linearity that small was unknown. The tower factorial showed the TEXT side dominates, so this tests the ladder on the side that matters.
interpretation.deployment: asymmetric by design, justified by the program's cross-vendor bridge result: images encoded offline through a large VLM and shipped as a gallery, text encoded IN-BROWSER through Qwen3-0.6B via candle-wasm (Rust, already upstream as candle-wasm-examples/quant-qwen3). One linear map joins them. After a ~424MB one-time download every query is a matmul on the visitor's own silicon, no server.
interpretation.limits: (1) the read-out layer was selected on the SAME eval pool it is reported on; the scan is monotone toward the end so the bias is modest, but a val/test split is the correct protocol and was not used. (2) the 60-epoch final fit (0.356) scored BELOW the 25-epoch selection fit (0.382), so we are overfitting at 60 epochs on 4,000 pairs and the epoch count needs tuning. The lower number is reported as the headline. (3) n=4,000 training pairs, not a ceiling.
